You are budding clowns looking to make a living through juggling, and the great clown Piolin is ready to teach you how to amaze the audience. Only one of you will be able to join the circus… and the show is about to begin! Malabares is a 18-card micro trick-taking game inspired by juggling. Players start with cards in hand, and some cards begin on the table representing what it's "in the air". A trick goes by playing cards in a must-follow fashion, and the numbers determine the order of drafting for the "in the air" cards. Players score depending of the circus card, that indicates if the show is going on day or night - knives score more during the day, torches at night. Players can also "shoot the moon" by performing the Piolin Move, getting a full hand of low-scoring cards. [Rating: 3/10] This one just didn't land. The way juggling is represented here, with certain cards going back into your hand and other cards staying on the table, felt convoluted and mechanical.

[Rating: 3/10] The rulebook is confusing and poorly structured, making it harder to learn than it should be. Once in play, the game offers very little player control, with outcomes driven largely by randomness rather than meaningful decisions. What seems intended as a clever use of a small card set instead turns into constant, unnecessary cycling, giving the impression of padding rather than elegance. Overall, the experience feels unfocused, repetitive, and far less satisfying than it promises.

[Rating: 5/10] Interesting attempt at a 3 player trick-taking game.  The rules are bit hard to understand. Reminded me a bit of the relatively unknown game Following Suit that I really enjoy, in that you're playing for 2 cards on the table and the card you win goes back into your hand.  The fact that game can play with a traditional deck and 2-5 players well means I'd always play that instead.

[Rating: 5/10] Trick taking game with main quirk is rotating cards between hands and table, but I think it still lacks something more for me.

[Rating: 6.5/10] Trick taking with less cards makes a not that hard to count cards and provide more enjoyable decisions. Did not understand the highest cards having the highest points, since you probably are going to "give" then to the last players, so you need to play then offsuit, which is very hard as you always get other cards. Played one rule wrong (transition from day to night), which change the outcome of the game but not the experience. Want to play again with all rules right.
